title: The Light of Kirpal
author: Kirpal Singh (1894-1974); questions by Western disciples

summary: Transcripts of informal question sessions at Sawan Ashram and Rajpur, 1969-71, in which Kirpal Singh goes round the room after sittings asking each Westerner what was seen and correcting them on the spot. Disciples report light of various colours, light that has grown dimmer, or nothing for days running; he replies with specific corrections (look into the middle of the light and it will open; do not visualise, it comes of itself; do not be anxious or make effort; the mind stands between). He ranks the colours (golden-yellow and white 'spiritual', red tied to a 'pushing attitude', blue as the common first light), gives the beginner's sequence of sky, stars, big star, moon, and uses the image of climbing a dark staircase to explain why many steps produce no light before the first glimpses.
why_relevant: First-person reports by practitioners with the teacher's immediate troubleshooting, including people who saw nothing; rare record of live correction rather than doctrine.

date_evidence.basis: Printing history in the saved text: 'First printing 1980, Second printing 1984, Third printing 1991, Fourth printing 1996'; Library of Congress Catalog Card No. 80-52357. Talks dated on ruhanisatsangusa.org chapter pages (e.g. ch. 38, Rajpur, 7 January 1971). archive.org metadata date 1969 is the date of the earliest talks.

notes: Rights: uploaded by Ruhani Satsang USA under Public Domain Mark 1.0, and Kirpal Singh disclaimed copyright in his works; the 1980 book is a Sant Bani Press transcription, so a cautious reader may prefer anchor + paraphrase over long quotation.
